title: runtime: seed settlement is not observable over HTTP — /health and /ready answer "ready" while the boot seed is still writing, and the banner's promised seed result is logged only at info level
body:
Found by a downstream app on the published 18.4.0 packages (steedos-labs/os-project-blackcat-crm#78, PR #82: a demo loader run from a second terminal placed orders before the seed had landed and costed 8 of 11 plans wrongly).

## Symptom

On `os dev` with an empty DB:
- `GET /api/v1/health` and `GET /api/v1/ready` answer `200 { status: ready, state: running }` from ~31 s, every second, while the inline boot seed is still writing in the background (measured: seeded customers land ~42–47 s, certifications and ratings ~99–120 s) and after it finishes — nothing distinguishes the two.
- Seed settlement is announced only over the `os dev` IPC channel (`serve.js` `announceSettled` → `process.send('objectstack:seed-settled')`), so a script or test in another process has no HTTP way to know when seeding is done.
- The CLI banner says seeding "continues in the background; its result prints after this banner" (`cli` `utils/format.js` ~1169), but the result is logged only at info level (`[Seeder] Data seeding complete.`, runtime `dist/index.js` ~21186); at the default log level nothing appeared in the 150 s after the seed landed.

## Why it matters

Every app that ships a demo/setup script, an e2e suite or a cloud health check against a fresh environment has to poll its own seeded row counts to know the data is there — a per-app reimplementation of a fact the runtime already knows.

## Suggested fix shape (for the lane to judge)

Expose seed settlement over HTTP (e.g. `/ready` reports `seed: pending | settled | failed`, or a dedicated readiness probe that waits for it), and print the seed result the banner promises at the level the banner implies.

Dedupe words: seed settlement http · ready seeding in flight · seed-settled ipc only · seed result banner info level.
